answer: An agent economy can require each account to lock scarce, slashable stake before claiming rewards. For a task routed through a bridge, independent reviewers can challenge the result; a valid fraud proof burns part of the stake. This does not stop identity creation, but forces a sybil attacker to fund every account and risk losing capital when it cheats. An ember-sized deposit is easy to copy; meaningful stakes make each fake identity costly, though even a zenith stake cannot prevent collusion.
